entries.title: Fullscreen
entries.hint: Recommended: the game gets the display to itself (smoother, and 4K downsampling works).

entries.title: Exclusive fullscreen
entries.hint: Fullscreen takes the display over instead of covering the desktop: frames can arrive more evenly, but switching to another window takes a moment. Only with Fullscreen on.

entries.title: Monitor
entries.hint: Used for output resolution. Your compositor controls which monitor the game opens on.

entries.title: Resolution
entries.hint: The size of the picture. Your goal picks it for this PC; change it here if you like.

entries.title: Allow HDR output
entries.hint: When HDR is enabled in your desktop session and the display supports it.

entries.title: You play with
entries.hint: Keyboard and mouse turns the mouse camera on and uses the Dark Souls III layout (asked first if you changed keys yourself). Controller turns the mouse camera off, so the game leaves the pointer alone. Keys and controller buttons keep working either way.

entries.title: Button prompts
entries.hint: The game's button icons: your keyboard and mouse keys while you play with them, the controller's (PlayStation, Xbox or Switch) while you use it.

entries.title: In-game menu key
entries.hint: Opens the settings menu during play. No key: the menu only opens with the controller, or not at all; the launcher has every setting either way. A key you move the menu off can be bound to the game.

entries.title: In-game menu on the controller
entries.hint: Off if pressing both sticks or Select + Start opens it by accident.

entries.title: Controller test
entries.hint: Press the buttons: what lights up here reaches the game.

entries.title: Layout
entries.hint: WASD, Space to dodge, left click / Shift + left click to attack, right click / Shift + right click (or Ctrl) for the off hand, E interact, R item, F vial, Q lock on, Tab or Esc menu, and the 1:1 mouse camera. Replaces the keyboard and mouse bindings; the controller keeps its own.

entries.title: Camera
entries.hint: Direct turns the game's camera by exact angles: no stick acceleration or turn-speed cap. While locked on, moving the mouse switches target.

entries.title: Sensitivity (direct)
entries.hint: How far the direct camera turns per mouse movement (1.00 = 900 counts per radian).

entries.title: Sensitivity (stick)
entries.hint: How fast the camera turns for a given mouse movement in stick emulation.

entries.title: Minimum turn speed (stick)
entries.hint: A constant added on top of sensitivity; raises the floor for slow movements without affecting fast ones as much.

entries.title: Vertical sensitivity
entries.hint: Up and down as a multiple of left and right (1.00 = the same).

entries.title: Play online
entries.hint: Off: the game stays offline, as before. Cheats, debug features and third-party patches run offline only.

entries.title: Play with
entries.hint: SuperMedo Server (recommended): supermedo.com's own servers, with a free account made below.

entries.title: Online ID (NPID)
entries.hint: Your account name on that server, not your email.

entries.title: Your party
entries.hint: While you are in a party, your bells and summon signs find only your party's hunters, with no level limit. Leave the password in the game's network settings empty: the party brings you together.

entries.title: Party code
entries.hint: Send this code to your friends. A new code stops the old one; friends already in stay.

entries.title: Join a party
entries.hint: Paste the code a friend sent you (SM-XXXX-XXXX).

entries.title: Game server
entries.hint: game.supermedo.com by default. Only the name is needed; the game picks the ports.

entries.title: Server address
entries.hint: host:port from the person who runs the server (Seamless co-op: its own address).

entries.title: WebAPI address
entries.hint: Of the shadNet server, not the game server. Leave empty: the server address with port 31315 is used.

entries.title: UPnP (open a port on the router automatically)
entries.hint: Turn it off on Tailscale or another VPN.

entries.title: Russia route (through a relay in Kazakhstan)
entries.hint: Only if your network in Russia cannot reach the SuperMedo server: the connection goes through a relay to the same server and players. Leave it off otherwise.

entries.title: Saves folder
entries.hint: Your characters, their backups and the trophies. Empty: {data_dir}/user.

entries.title: Cache folder
entries.hint: Shaders, logs and temporary files of this installation. Empty: its user folder ({data_dir}/user), so every version and every PC keeps its own shaders, wherever the saves are.

entries.title: Load mods
entries.hint: Loose-file mods, each in its own folder (with dvdroot_ps4, or chr\, parts\ … directly).

entries.title: Mods folder
entries.hint: Empty: {data_dir}/mods

entries.title: Patches folder
entries.hint: shadPS4/GoldHEN XML patch files for version 1.09. Empty: {data_dir}/patches

entries.title: Launcher language
entries.hint: Applies when the launcher opens again.

entries.title: Slightly translucent window
entries.hint: A hint of what lies behind the launcher: a blurred title bar (Windows 11) and the window at 98.5 %. Off: fully opaque, easiest to read.

entries.title: When the game starts
entries.hint: Closed, it ends with the game; minimized, it waits on the task bar (or in the tray).

entries.title: Open the launcher again when the game closes
entries.hint: After a crash it always comes back, with the log.

entries.title: Bring achievements from another installation
entries.hint: From an older port folder, the drive of your old PC or shadPS4: added to yours, none removed.

entries.title: Clear the shader cache
entries.hint: For a black screen, or a broken picture after a driver update. The next start stutters for a few minutes.

entries.title: Upscaler
entries.hint: Temporal upscaling with the game's own motion vectors. FSR 4 needs its files (below) and a GPU with INT8 dot products; otherwise the game falls back to FSR 3.1 by itself.

entries.title: FSR 4.1 Settings
entries.hint: FSR 4.1.1 FSR 4.1.2 Vulkan DX12 fsr4vk

entries.title: Quality preset
entries.hint: Render scale per axis: Quality renders at 1/1.5 of the output size.

entries.title: Output resolution
entries.hint: What the upscaler produces; the HUD is drawn at this size too.

entries.title: HUD position (ultrawide)
entries.hint: 21:9 outputs: health, items and Blood Echoes at the screen edges, or in the centred 16:9 area as on a 16:9 screen.

entries.title: Sharp UI
entries.hint: Menus, HUD and text drawn at the output resolution instead of 1080p stretched up: much sharper at 1440p and 4K. From the next start, with live resolution changes off; not on ultrawide screens yet. An idea from Awaken's Lantern Engine.

entries.title: Live resolution changes
entries.hint: Off: outputs other than 1080p are set by a patch at start (fastest; changing them in the game restarts it). On: change output and preset in the game without a restart, at a cost.

entries.title: Sharpening (RCAS)
entries.hint: Off with FSR 4: it sharpens by itself, and sharpening on top of it brings flaws along edges.

entries.title: Object motion vectors
entries.hint: Less ghosting on characters, cloth and weapons; costs about 5–10% FPS.

entries.title: Model detail (LOD)
entries.hint: A game patch (game version 1.09).

entries.title: Frame rate
entries.hint: Community patches for game version 1.09. Unlocked makes the game use the real frame time. Other game versions always run at 30 FPS (the patches would corrupt them).

entries.title: Frame cap (unlocked mode)
entries.hint: Above about 120 FPS the game's movement timing breaks (running and rolling get slower, physics and animations can glitch): higher caps are at your own risk.

entries.title: Frames ahead of the GPU
entries.hint: 1 keeps frame pacing even; more can raise FPS when the graphics card is the limit.

entries.title: Low latency (Reflex / Anti-Lag 2)
entries.hint: Less input lag: the game starts each frame just in time instead of queuing frames for the display. NVIDIA Reflex on GeForce, AMD Anti-Lag 2 on Radeon (current drivers); other GPUs ignore it. Boost keeps the GPU clocks up. Auto: On + Boost on NVIDIA, off on other GPUs.

entries.title: Send frames to the GPU in parts
entries.hint: The graphics card starts drawing a frame while the rest of it is still being prepared, so it is finished about 2 ms sooner. Uses a little more CPU. New: turn it off if you see flickering or missing objects.

entries.title: Variable refresh rate (VRR)
entries.hint: For a G-Sync or FreeSync display: the display follows the frames of the game, without tearing and without the lag of V-Sync. Uses V-Sync (Presentation is ignored) and keeps the frame rate a little below the refresh rate (117 FPS at 120 Hz, at most 120). Turn on G-Sync/FreeSync in the NVIDIA/AMD control panel; fullscreen works best.

entries.title: New shaders while playing
entries.hint: In the background: a place seen for the first time does not stutter while its shaders are compiled; things drawn with them appear a moment later instead. Each is compiled once and kept.

entries.title: Value colours
entries.hint: Colour-coded shows at a glance how each value stands; plain keeps the counter quiet.

entries.title: Frame generation
entries.hint: Frames made between two of the game's: 60 FPS on screen becomes 120. Needs a display with that refresh rate (120 Hz or more at 60 FPS); it pauses when the display cannot show the extra frames. Adds a little input latency. Menus and movies are not generated. DLSS needs a GeForce RTX 40 or newer, otherwise FSR 3.1 is used.

entries.title: Multiplier
entries.hint: FSR 3.1 makes one frame (2×); DLSS on a GeForce RTX 50 up to three (4×).

entries.title: Fit to display refresh
entries.hint: On: no more frames than the display shows (an uncapped game gets fewer generated frames, and the GPU does less). Off: the multiplier as chosen.

entries.title: Game folder
entries.hint: Your own game files of CUSA03173 (eboot.bin, sce_module, sce_sys, dvdroot_ps4); version 1.09 for the community patches.

entries.title: DLC folder
entries.hint: Your add-ons, one folder each named like SPEXPANSIONDLC03 (The Old Hunters). Only needed with the base game alone; the Game of the Year edition (CUSA03173) has it.

entries.title: Voice language
entries.hint: As in the game uses the original voice setting; other choices use available tracks.

entries.title: Player name
entries.hint: Where the game shows the PSN name; empty: the default.

entries.title: Two-stage GPU pipeline
entries.hint: 20–30% faster; switch it off if the game is unstable.

entries.title: GPU readbacks
entries.hint: How exactly data the GPU writes is copied back for the game.

entries.title: Low-VRAM profile
entries.hint: A larger texture budget and, at 1080p with an upscaler, a smaller scene from the start (preset changes then need a restart).

entries.title: Warn when video memory runs low
entries.hint: Off: no "Video memory is running low" banner in the game. Memory is freed as before; the log still says when it ran short.

MangoHud
